newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei ends directionless session firmer.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei ends directionless session firmer.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market"s key index finished higher on Wednesday after directionless trade for most of the day. Brokers said the market was now focusing on chemical and steel shares, due to expected solid earnings.
But some major blue-chip issues, which had bolstered the market recently, were hurt by profit-taking, brokers said.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 average gained 128.37 points or 0.69 percent to close at 18,599.12. Its March futures were 150 points higher at 18,650.
The broader-based TOPIX index ended down 0.88 points or 0.06 percent at 1,380.24.
Turnover was 447 million shares on Wednesday, up from

"The higher turnover suggests that the range of buying is widening. But I don"t think the trend of two-tier investment has changed," said Koichi Ichiko, general manager of the securities investment department at Asahi Mutual Life Insurance Co.

The recent rally in blue-chip issues spilled over to lower-priced shares in sectors such as steel and chemical. But construction and banking shares remained weak and reduced stock gains overall, brokers said.
Some brokers said that the Nikkei average was pushed higher ahead of the close by domestic securities houses" buying orders for themselves and by investment trusts.
Declining issues outnumbered gainers 570 to 492, while 183 issues were unchanged.

Of the lower-priced shares that attracted interest, major Japanese chemical maker Showa Denko KK was actively pursued. Its shares gained 17 yen to 275 yen in a volume of 8.233 million, the third heaviest on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
Showa Denko was supported by a rise in the firm"s annual profits announced earlier this week, brokers said.
Shares of Kawasaki Heavy Industries Ltd, a major shipbuilder, rose 17 yen to end at 523 yen in a volume of 4.586 million.
"Shipbuilders like Kawasaki Heavy have lagged behind steel and chemical shares," said a broker at a major Japanese securities house.
Shares in the construction and banking sectors remained weak, brokers said.
Many issues in the construction sector 0#CON.T hit their lows for this financial year, dragged down by a report that the government would review its public works spending plan.

A survey by private research company Teikoku Databank Ltd released earlier this week also hurt the shares. It said the amount of debts guaranteed by 98 Japanese general contractors totalled 3.22 trillion yen at the end of September 1996, which was down by only 3.4 percent from the end of March 1996.
Kumagai Gumi Co ended down 15 yen at 169 yen, making it the biggest percentage loser on the first section. It earlier fell to 165 yen, a low for the fiscal 1996/97 year.
Aoki Corp ended down six yen at 150 yen, Fujita Corp lost eight to 180 yen and Hazama Corp eased six to end at 249 yen. All three hit lows for the financial year this morning.

Shares in long-term credit banks also fell in heavy trade. Brokers said that sentiment for the banks was hurt by a announcement by Moody"s Investors Service on Tuesday that it may downgrade the banks" senior debt ratings.
Shares in Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) lost three yen to 225 yen. The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) fell 50 yen to 1,370 yen.
By sector, gainers were led by transportation equipment, food, air transportation, pulp/paper, fisheries and shipbuilding. Losers were led by credit/lease, precision instruments and real estate.
The second section index ended down 11.20 points at 1,726.89, with 6.79 million shares traded.
The over-the-counter (OTC) index fell 6.57 points to 1,217.88.
-- Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8027
